sources.review_note: Organization dry-run target selection has all-repository and capped selected-repository branches. Selection and clicking Run describe a procedure, not observed execution or adoption of a testing obligation.

The validity table distinguishes provider-confirmed active, unsupported or unverifiable unknown, and inactive. Unknown cannot substitute for inactive; an inactive token still leaves possible past unauthorized access to investigate. Column labels and product substitutions describe the table rather than new controls.

Bypass has distinct repository/organization/enterprise alert, audit, and conditional email effects. Watcher qualifications restrict receipt; a secret link and bypass reason need sensitive handling. These effects do not establish revocation or completed remediation.

The Next.js page embeds a React table inside two contexts and loads middleware data, with an empty-array fallback. Page plumbing and UI namespace selection are implementation references, not evidence that an empty result is a clean scan.

Each contributor-selected bypass reason determines an alert state. Closed test/false-positive alerts record the selected classification, and an open fix-later alert retains remediation work. State transition alone cannot prove harmlessness.
The request-decision email follows review, but can report denial as well as approval; neither actual delivery nor accepted bypass was observed.
The feature file declares fpt/ghec wildcard branches and GHES >=3.20. These pinned documentation predicates constrain partner-validity rendering, not live entitlement or token-validation execution.
The enterprise dry-run fragment caps selection at ten repositories and separately requires Run. It cannot establish whole-enterprise coverage or test completion.

The synchronization workflow is docs-internal-only, scheduled on weekdays and manually dispatchable. Write permissions, bot-token use, pinned actions, automated approval/auto-merge, concurrency, and failure routing describe this upstream pipeline, not a locally authorized rollout or independent review.
The fpt/ghec wrapper limits automatic partner scanning to public repositories and public npm packages. Partner alerts go to providers; this does not establish repository user-alert visibility.

New-alert recipients depend on alert access and preferences, with a commit-author exception. Email additionally requires watching, activity/security subscriptions, and the email channel; the included assignee fragment separately adds assigned-alert notifications.

Enterprise bypass configuration requires enabled push protection, then an explicitly chosen actor list. Secret teams are unavailable for that list. Included navigation, configuration steps, and octicon accessibility attributes are contextual UI evidence, not actor authorization or coverage proof.
The bypass URL is bound to the pushing user and the source specifies 404 for another user. This is a documented identity condition, not a request made or a broadly adopted access policy.
Wiki scanning is cloud-renderable and requires GHES >3.18 in this feature metadata. The strict greater-than predicate must not be broadened to >=3.18.

The merge rule requires resolved alerts for one or more selected provider/custom/generic groups. It supports prevention only for the selected scope; resolved-alert state does not itself prove credential rotation.
The GHES-only note labels management endpoints public preview and changeable. Product/release variables and conditional boundaries preserve applicability without attesting API availability.

Only published patterns expose enablement, organization repositories need push protection enabled, and common patterns can disrupt contributors. Organization pattern configuration is not proof of effective repository blocking.

This feature describes multi-repository/public-leak indicators on fpt/ghec and a Team-plan expansion comment. Tracking references and comments are pinned metadata, not reviewed issue bodies or current commercial entitlement.
Auditing alert-response actions is a documented capability. The linked audit page remains distinct; auditability does not itself establish retention, collected events, or an actual investigation.

Enterprise custom-pattern protection requires enterprise-level push protection; common patterns risk disruption. This is a conditional prerequisite and tradeoff, not permission to enable a feature across an estate.
The pencil action edits the identified custom pattern in its owning scope. Pattern selection is navigation and does not establish global enablement.

The chart separates absolute/percentage metrics, provider recommendations, enterprise settings, and organization inheritance. Recommended defaults are not local policy; an uneditable enterprise column does not prevent an organization override through its separate setting.

Generic-pattern availability differs across fpt, ghec, and ghes and depends on organization ownership and Secret Protection. Data substitutions, links, and ifversion guards retain the actual branches; a link is not inherited review of its destination.

The product fragment distinguishes automatic free public scanning, enabled protection for organization private/internal repositories, and managed/enterprise user-owned cases. Static capability flags cannot establish enrollment or permissions.

Within the exemptions feature gate, trusted automation is the intended use, but the source warns exemptions may leak secrets and urges caution. Reduced friction is a design motive, not grounds to bypass prevention without an accountable decision.

The article API tests are authored expectations rather than execution receipts. The provider-header regex contains alternation and admits empty matches; section checks are conditional. The comment-stripper dependency confirms unclosed comment openers can survive.

The GHES3.18 source lacks the metadata and Base64 keys throughout the digest-matched dataset. Whole-source key-absence inspection reuses previously independently verified provider cells; absence is preserved as unknown, not explicit unsupported behavior.
New pattern starts organization creation. It is not editing, publication, enforcement, or an observed creation receipt.

The cloud feature describes public leak locations and deduplicated-alert repositories in public beta. Source comments and tracking identifiers do not establish current availability or ingestion of their linked discussions.

Custom pattern creation requires a name and regex, offers extra constraints, and directs sample matching. Sample testing is useful prevention preparation but not exhaustive precision/recall coverage; version-specific screenshots remain uninspected assets.

The JSON endpoint chooses fpt by default, derives a dataset path, serves raw parsed data with separate browser/shared-cache periods, and catches errors as 404. Unlike middleware it does not resolve Liquid, so consumers cannot read all raw strings as effective booleans.
Full exemption is a feature-gated actor-menu operation. It describes a bypass option and its UI metadata, not an adopted requirement to grant exemptions.
Merge protection is a public-preview description with cloud wildcard predicates and GHES >=3.24. This is a pinned feature scope, not proof of effective merge rejection on a repository.

Older and legacy token patterns can be outside push protection because of false-positive risk; Azure Storage Keys illustrate recent-token support. No universal token-generation coverage can be inferred.

GHES instance enablement by a site administrator precedes use, and enterprise policy can restrict repository toggles. These are prerequisites and inheritance constraints, not actual deployment or scope acceptance.

The GHES3.20 digest-matched dataset contains no extended-metadata key. Existing provider-cell verification is reused; only the separately checked absence proposition gains this review, and missing support data is not false.

AI regex assistance is gated, requires no Copilot subscription, and AI-detected availability is scoped to organization/enterprise repositories with Secret Protection. Generator assistance, detection availability, and commercial subscription are separate facts.

Transformer tests mock loader/template data and test GHES/free-product conditional evaluation. They cannot certify every real dataset row, live product behavior, or the success of an unexecuted test run.
Push-protection metrics are explicitly preview and subject to change. Variable substitution names the feature/release phase; this is not a stable measurement contract or observed result.
The optional full-exemption step is feature-gated and actor-specific. The menu and icon describe an available action; optionality must not become a universal policy obligation.

The synchronizer requires a token, parses and schema-checks fetched YAML, preserves relative paths, and writes local files before entry calls main. The upstream main branch and helper remain dependencies; none of this source code was executed.

The displayed dry-run sample is capped at 1000. Reviewing false positives and retesting changed patterns supports prevention; the sample is not the full-match denominator and the screenshot is not a run receipt.

The subject README is maintenance documentation with discrepancies: daily versus weekday scheduling, Liquid prose versus React display, enabled versus supported protection, outdated dataset names/paths, and human review versus automated approval. Preserve the discrepancy instead of silently accepting the README as execution truth.

Custom-pattern push protection is optional, applies only to enrolled repositories, and may disrupt contributors. Choosing Enable is not proof of adoption or blocking; screenshot references remain descriptive.
The stylesheet sets a minimum menu width. It is display implementation, not a security obligation or an executed accessibility result.
Public monitoring is preview and changeable; the discussion link invites feedback. Reading the invitation grants no authority to send private findings or claim current availability.
The GHES3.15 digest-matched dataset omits metadata and Base64 keys. Full-source absence inspection reuses existing verified cells and preserves unknown separately from unsupported.

User protection is feature-gated. Repository secret scanning requires a bypass reason, while user protection on public repositories without it may allow bypass with no reason and no alert; blocking coverage remains limited to supported secrets.

Alert taxonomy is version-dependent: cloud adds partner alerts sent directly to participating providers; user and push-protection alerts are repository-visible. A missing partner alert in a repository view is not a clean-scan result.
A bypass request comment records a contributor explanation or claimed safety. It neither grants approval nor independently establishes that a value is safe.
Checking pushes for custom patterns is a configurable scanning capability. The product-name substitution supplies a label rather than a new detection guarantee.
File-upload protection in the web UI is preview and subject to change. The source label is pinned reference context, not a current-release guarantee.
The GHES3.16 digest-matched dataset omits metadata and Base64 keys. Existing provider rows are reused without new review credit; absent keys must retain unknown semantics.

Repository or organization push protection can prevent pushes of detected secrets when enabled. This supports a prevention mechanism within its coverage; it does not establish enrollment, bypass absence, or rotation of an already exposed credential.

Participating providers receive public-repository/npm detections, validate strings, and choose revocation/replacement/contact by risk. Public partner configuration is fixed, and regular alerts follow a different route. Provider notice alone cannot prove revocation.
Custom patterns are described for organization-owned Team/Enterprise repositories with Secret Protection. The product fragment does not assert personal-repository parity or authorize activation.
AI generic detection is declared for cloud and GHES >=3.23. Tracking/Team comments remain metadata; neither detection quality nor current entitlements follow from the predicate.
The enterprise REST API can enable or disable named security products. This is capability reference, not execution authority or evidence that a feature was changed.
The article template outputs title, conditional intro, and content. Output structure is not provider support, native enforcement, or rendered-page assurance.
The config gives a specific target filename and separate upstream SHA/blob identities. Those stored identifiers do not substitute for the GitHub Docs pin or proof of current remote synchronization.
Delegated alert closure has a GA comment, cloud branches, and GHES >=3.18. Closing permission and release metadata are not authorization for a particular actor or proof of remediation.
User-owned scanning metadata names GHEC-EMU and GHES >=3.13 and calls it public beta. It does not extend to unrestricted personal cloud repositories or certify a current release.
Extended metadata checks are preview and changeable. This caveat constrains reliance on returned fields without creating a new mandatory setting.
Enterprise/organization per-pattern configuration is preview and changeable. Feature labels do not establish target configuration or governance acceptance.
Publish pattern is an explicit post-review operation. Dry-run completion, publication, and effective protection remain separate stages.

The schema/type definition separates required and optional fields, allows strings for support fields, and uses an unanchored identifier regex. TypeScript Base64/duplicate requirements differ from runtime validation. Schema acceptance cannot certify strict booleans or target capability.

The loader caches by absolute path and returns clones, but parses YAML without schema checking and turns nullish data into an empty array. Empty data is a loader fallback, not measured absence of supported secrets.

The support reference separates category capabilities, plan/feature gates, precision estimates, token versions, and generated UI dependencies. Generic validity and password blocking/validity are unsupported; provider support is partial. Table facts here are reused context and do not add provider-cell review credit.
User push protection is declared only for fpt/ghec in this pin. The missing GHES branch is documentation scope rather than proof of every possible server behavior.
Organization custom configuration must enable protection before specifying bypass actors. Included navigation and icon attributes do not prove actor approval, inheritance, or repository coverage.

Middleware matches a configured suffix, checks request context/version, selects version data, and declines unknown server versions. It resolves only validity/metadata Liquid and appends duplicate links; other string fields retain truthiness hazards.
User-owned alert details and token metadata require repository admin access. Enterprise owners may request temporary access; ownership alone is not permission or actual grant.
The web UI blocks a supported secret only in a protected repository and shows its location. The documentation is not a target UI inspection or proof of every file-upload/version path.

Contributor bypass classification determines alert closure/notification or retained open state. Closed test/false-positive classifications remain assertions, and fix-later notifications leave credential response work unresolved.
The scanned-surface list includes issue/pull-request/discussion content, gated wikis, and secret gists. It describes detection scope, not measured scan completion or guaranteed recall on any surface.
Only published patterns expose the protection-enable option. Publication is therefore a prerequisite, not proof of protection enablement.

Scope reference retains public-monitoring attribution, paired-file limitations, cross-product legacy-token gaps, and blocking limitations: timeouts, five-item display, >1000 existing secrets, and cloud public pushes >50 MB. Post-push alerts are detection after prevention failure.
Metrics filters select repository scope and time range; the date is bypass time, not detection time. Search filters do not replace the disclosed denominator or establish remediation outcome.
Extended metadata feature metadata includes cloud and GHES >=3.23. Its version gate differs from validity support and does not prove token metadata was retrieved.
The three bypass reasons are contributor classifications. They do not constitute an independent safety determination or rotation/revocation evidence.
Middleware conditional tests use mocked data and expected booleans in product contexts. They describe intended evaluation and do not certify all real provider cells or executed tests.
Validity enablement is a repository settings procedure. Included navigation/product labels preserve its context; the instruction is neither an activation receipt nor a universal adopted setting.
Rendering tests expect a successful redirected page and no 500 for malformed double-version URLs. These are authored assertions, not a complete content/capability or actual run certificate.
Custom-pattern checks before default-branch merge are separately configurable. The linked lifecycle procedure is a dependency, not evidence of activation.

The React component preserves records through filters/sorting/pagination and maps literal keys to translated alert/support labels. Truthiness collapses absence and nonempty strings into icons. Search analytics invokes a bounded heuristic sanitizer, whose source was read; that is not proof of arbitrary-secret redaction.

The access fragment lists owners/managers/admins for the surrounding alert context. It does not itself establish access to a particular private alert, scope-wide enrollment, or a clean scan when permission is missing.

The GHES3.14 dataset lacks metadata, Base64, and duplicate-marker keys throughout. Full-source absence checks preserve unknown; the previously verified provider cells remain unchanged and receive no new credit.

The concept page distinguishes history detection, periodic rescanning, repository alerts, provider notification, custom/AI features, and optional public monitoring. Its direct instruction to rotate after alert supports credential response; history cleanup cannot replace revocation.

The variable file defines names, conditional labels, CTA markup, and explicitly dummy learner examples. Display strings are not capability/financial evidence, CTA maintenance is contextual documentation, and dummy snippets are not live credential exposure.

Per-pattern enterprise/organization toggles, scope-limited metrics, changing recommended defaults, and organization overrides are separate mechanisms. An inherited or recommended default is not an adopted effective protection policy.
Scanning entire present Git history/all branches describes capability. It does not prove a run completed or include branches absent from the repository.
Resolved-alert merge protection is preview and changeable. The variables name a rule/release phase, not effective enforcement or security review acceptance.

The Markdown transformer has an independent version-loading/evaluation path, preserves every row, and converts truthy values to symbols. Missing files become empty data; absent optional fields become crosses. Cleanup/template logic is implementation evidence, not unsupported capability certification.
Within ghec, enterprise policy governs whether organizations can toggle generic detection and defaults to allowed. Allowed is permission to configure, not enabled detection or local policy adoption.

Repository enablement or push triggers scanning against provider patterns and conditional enterprise-cloud/server custom patterns. Alerts describe detection effects, not completed prevention or incident response.
Submit request is a requester action only. It cannot establish approved bypass or a successful push.
Checking email is a notification procedure. No mailbox, delivery, reviewer decision, or completed bypass was observed.
The GHES3.19 dataset lacks extended metadata. The full-source key check reuses previously verified provider cells and preserves absent fields without an unsupported conclusion.

The summary has ordered wiki-feature and older-GHES branches for non-code surfaces alongside all-history scanning. Tokens/private keys are examples; conditionals cannot be flattened into universal wiki support.
The GHES3.17 dataset lacks metadata and Base64 fields throughout. Existing cells are reused and absence remains distinct from false and rendered No.
AI custom-pattern generation is cloud-only in this feature file with a limited-public-beta description. Tracking and Team-plan comments are not current entitlement or generation-quality proof.
The security/quality tab is the documented repository alert location. A location statement does not prove delivery, access, or resolution.
Multi-ref pushes can be blocked due to unintended refs. Timed-out push scanning may still scan afterward; post-push detection cannot establish that prevention succeeded.
Privately exposed-secret reporting is preview and subject to change. Naming a report capability does not attest a report, revocation, or actual incident response.

Organization/enterprise delegated bypass disables repository bypass settings. Repository protection precedes selecting allowed roles/teams, with secret teams excluded. Navigation and actor-list UI are not local permission/adoption decisions.

The feature-gated user-owned fragment nests ghec/ghes availability and grammar branches. Public-preview wording and EMU restrictions remain attached; grammatical substitutions are metadata, not security requirements.

AI generic detection is gated and does not require a Copilot subscription, but AI-detected availability requires organization/enterprise ownership plus Secret Protection. Product names and guards preserve distinctions without promising recall.
Bypass email depends on owner/manager/admin opt-in. No email cannot establish no bypass, and notification is not credential remediation.

Public-monitoring feature metadata permits fpt/ghec rendering, but the linked concept product clause limits eligibility to Enterprise Cloud with security features and excludes data residency. Render scope and entitlement are different.
Enterprise secret-scanning metrics metadata includes cloud and GHES >3.13. These version predicates and issue comments do not establish measured metrics or response outcomes.
The report/revocation feature description is cloud-only and GitHub-PAT-specific. One-click capability, tracking references, and Team-plan comments are not a completed report or revocation receipt.
The route reexports the page implementation and its server-side function. Route wiring is a source dependency, not scanning enforcement.

Playwright fixtures describe keyboard, width, heading, naming, row-header, narrow-view, and contrast expectations. They were inspected inertly, not executed; fixture assertions are not all-version accessibility certification.
Custom-pattern navigation follows the scope that created the pattern. Repository/organization settings and enterprise policy UI are references, not proof of actual permissions or global enablement.
Paired-secret detection needs both components in the same file, reducing false positives while missing isolated partial pairs. This capability limit must not become a clean-secret conclusion.

Dry runs require repository administration, and enterprise owners need an organization-owner role for the described cross-organization access. No role was granted and ownership is not assumed to confer access.

AI assistance requires a pattern name and explicit prompt/example/result selection; manual regex remains available. Language preference, optional constraints, and test-string population do not validate generated rules or authorize real-secret input.
